response.rationale: Markedly elevated troponin, dynamic ECG changes with Q waves and ST shifts, and coronary occlusions confirm acute myocardial infarction (MI). Acute coronary syndrome (R1) is broader and less specific; coronary artery disease (R2) is an underlying etiology, not the acute event.

rejected.why: Coronary artery disease is a chronic condition and does not capture the acute myocardial necrosis and infarction.
Acute coronary syndrome includes unstable angina and MI; given the troponin elevation and ECG/cath findings, MI is the more precise and clinically appropriate diagnosis.
